git_rationale.root_cause_commit: ed4b15bb8 feat(codex): F2 third tid-bind + persistence.ts atomic write + CLAUDE.md doc fix
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: clearDaemonState() was given lock file deletion responsibility it does not own. When it runs before releaseDaemonLock(), the lock file gets deleted while the daemon still holds an open file descriptor — a window opens for another process to create a new lock at the same path, and releaseDaemonLock() then deletes the new process's lock.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Lock lifecycle now owned exclusively by acquireDaemonLock / releaseDaemonLock. clearDaemonState() only deletes daemonStateFile. Stale lock cleanup is covered by acquireDaemonLock's retry loop.

blast_radius_declarations.reason: controlClient.ts imports clearDaemonState() but clearDaemonState's behavior change (no longer deletes lock) only affects the caller if it depended on lock deletion — it does not. controlClient.ts:189 calls cleanupDaemonState() which wraps clearDaemonState(); the removal of lock deletion is strictly narrowing behavior. AC3 confirms the fix. No regression possible.

Integration test uses clearDaemonState() at lines 323 and 358 for test cleanup only. Removing lock deletion from clearDaemonState() means tests no longer implicitly delete the lock — which is correct: tests should call releaseDaemonLock() explicitly if they hold the lock. No test behavior is broken; the prior implicit side-effect was the bug.
